doc.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Naivety about the acoustic bass and a fiberglass school bass
summary: Being young he saw the acoustic bass as an oversized electric bass and was unafraid; the school bass was fiberglass.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Is it more of a physical challenge to play the acoustic bass?

I think being as young and naive as I was at the age of eleven I wasn’t aware of the level of intimidation I should have had at that time. I just thought of it as being an oversized electric bass. So when I went to junior high school I just said oh, well, you know, I’ll just do what I do at home. You know I didn’t realize the switch that I should have been thinking about. But I think in that case it worked in my favor, because I wasn’t scared of it.
I hope you didn’t have one of those typical junior high instruments where the strings are two inches off the —
Oh, yea, of course. Fiberglass. A fiberglass bass.
Well you must have developed a lot of strength.
